Cyan Clayworks: Courses - Cyan Clayworks Skip to content Our courses run throughout the year; taster classes, daytime and evening courses running over several weeks, and one/two day workshops. The taster sessions are ideal for complete beginners who would like to try one or two techniques. Absolutely no prior experience needed! We often run specialist one or two day workshops on Saturdays. These may focus on wheelthrowing and handbuilding, or monoprinting for example, allowing students to build their confidence in a particular area. We finish and fire your pieces ready to collect at a later date. The longer courses are usually suitable for beginners and/or those with some prior experience, and we run occasional intermediate level courses. Students will be able to try a wide range of techniques and find which ones that suit them best. For those who’ve worked with clay before we can go into more depth at the different stages of making; help you with creative decision-making, thinking about the relationship between the form and surface and much more. Depending on the individual course, the focus can be on different areas of ceramics, such as functional pots, coilbuilding, slabbuilding and surface decoration using slips and glazes. All of our courses have strictly limited numbers, and usually both of us are teaching to give everyone more input. Fiona specialises in handbuilding and the surface; Chris mainly in throwing and functional pots. All materials, use of tools/equipment and firings are included. Everything is prepped for you in advance and we have a range of coloured slips and glazes mixed by ourselves. Our approach to teaching is fairly hands-on and supportive, but without being too prescriptive – you can choose what you make. Each technique is demonstrated by us at the start of the class, and we can point you in the direction of other relevant artists and makers as appropriate for inspiration. We have a contemporary approach to ceramics, but also have a broad knowledge of its history. Cyan Clayworks is a ‘working’ studio where we both create and sell ceramics; you can look at and handle our work in the shop space, and often see pieces in progress. There are lots of books and journals in the studio for inspiration too. Both of us have trained in ceramics to post-graduate level, have been working professionally since the 1990s, and are highly committed to this creative field, and so we have a lot to offer our students in a friendly environment. We are occasionally asked if we offer any discounts for students or retirees. Unfortunately as we are a small non-profit studio we are unable to offer discounts- we keep our prices as low as they can be. Additionally we are not able to accommodate those under 16 or those with complex support needs; for health & safety and insurance reasons. Each team was encouraged to explore a live community issue, engage with relevant organisations or community assets, and develop a practical response that could improve awareness, access, participation or support.The structure of the programme included an introductory session on social innovation, team formation by Edinburgh district, community research and validation, and a final showcase. Session 7 included a reflective walk up Calton Hill, helping students view their districts in the wider city context and consider what community partners had identified as important. Tiphereth Calendar: Craft Workshops Skip to main content Summer Fayre Saturday 20 June 2026 10am - 2pm Join us for a wonderful celebration of community, nature, and hands-on making. As part of this year's Summer Fayre, we are hosting an incredible line-up of creative, bite-sized workshops across our beautiful grounds. Whether you fancy getting stuck into pottery, trying your hand at traditional textile crafts, or building a home for garden wildlife, there is a session for everyone. All of our workshops are completely beginner-friendly, and all materials are fully provided. Please Note: Our workshops are suitable for both adults and children. To ensure safety with tools, hot glue, and needles, children under 10 must be accompanied by an adult. Explore the sessions below and visit the workshop to book a space, Plant Sales Home Baking Food Stalls Craft Sales Click map to open Click to open Open Craft Workshops Visit our workshops today and book a slot. Bird Box Building £25 Visit Green Keepers Barn - Number 4 on the map Experience the joy of woodworking in a condensed, stress-free environment! The Pentland Group invites you into the Greenkeepers workshop for a fun, wood work taster session. Build your own bird box. We have taken care of all the measuring and heavy sawing so you can get straight to the best parts: building and decorating. You will piece together the pre-cut sides, front, and back before selecting your favorite roof style—options include rustic larch or traditional felt. After assembly, spend the rest of the hour personalising your bird box by painting, carving prepared wood, or shaping custom wooden plaques to attach to the front. Wet Felting £10 Visit 'The May' - Number 10 on the map Dive into a colourful, sensory crafting experience with our introductory wet felting session! In just 45 minutes, you will transform raw, incredibly soft Merino wool into a one-of-a-kind piece of textile art. The session is wonderfully hands-on: you will start by blending your favourite wool colours, then layer them into a unique pattern on a bamboo mat. Next comes the magic—using warm water and skin-friendly olive soap, you will roll and agitate the wool until the fibres interlock perfectly. You’ll leave the session with a gorgeous 20cm x 20cm felted artwork to take home and display. Embroidery £10 Visit The May - Number 10 on the map Looking for a quick spark of creativity? Join us for an engaging 45-minute craft session where you will learn a unique and playful technique for creating textured, three-dimensional textile art! This introductory class is perfect for complete beginners, families, and anyone looking to try something new in a relaxed, supportive environment. During the session, you will use a hot glue gun to "sketch" a small, raised design directly onto your fabric. Once set, you will use colorful embroidery thread to sew over your glue outline, creating a vibrant, puffed-out 3D masterpiece. Screen Printing - Canvas Tote Bag £15 Visit The Print Studio - Number 1 on the map Ever wanted to try your hand at screen printing? Skip the flat world of digital prints and come experience the incredibly satisfying, tactile world of traditional printmaking in our dedicated workshop. Enjoy a taster session where you will get the full creator experience. Explore our selection of screens, choose the perfect design, and pick your custom color palette. From flooding the screen to pulling the ink, you’ll be in control of the entire printing process. By the end of the session, you’ll have mastered the basics of pulling a perfect print and created a stylish, personalised canvas tote bag that’s ready to take away. Seed Sowing and Pot Decorating £5 Visit The Grarden - Number 7 on the map Unleash your inner artist and gardener all in one go! Join us for a fun, creative session where you’ll transform a humble terracotta pot into a vibrant piece of living art. You’ll start on the crafty side, using our selection of colorful paints and designs to decorate your pot exactly how you like—whether you prefer bold patterns, cute illustrations, or classic garden styles. Once painted the planting begins! You'll fill your new pot with seed compost and select your favorite seeds to sow. It's the ultimate "grow-your-own" keepsake that keeps on giving. Herbal Tea Worksop £10 Visit the Garden Group - Number 7 on the mapSlow down, awaken your senses, and discover the incredible flavors hiding in the garden patch. Our Herbal Tea Making Workshop invites you to explore the journey of herbs from root to teacup in a cozy, interactive setting. Using dried herbs carefully collected from our very own grounds, we will guide you through an immersive tasting experience. You’ll sip and discover the unique qualities of classic blends like soothing chamomile, vibrant rose, and nutrient-rich nettle. Alongside the tasting, you will receive beautifully illustrated information leaflets packed with facts on each plant. Best of all, you'll pack up a custom tea sample to enjoy at home, and our Walled Garden will be open afterward with plants available to buy so you can jumpstart your own backyard tea garden! Ceramic Painting £10 Visit The Pottery - Number 9 on the map Add a personal, handmade touch to your home decor or create a unique gift in this sweet, half-hour pottery painting session. We supply a pre-made, bisque-fired ceramic hanging ornaments, leaving the best part entirely up to you. Whether you want to paint a colorful seasonal decoration, a vibrant pattern, or a personalised mini-sign, we have all the colors and tools ready to bring your idea to life. It’s a wonderful, relaxing micro-crafting experience. Mug Decorating £22 Visit The Pottery - Number 7 on the map Upgrade your kitchen cupboard with a mug that has a real story behind it! Step into our creative space for a cozy, 1-hour pottery painting workshop where you get to be the designer. We will provide a pre-made, bisque-fired mugs, leaving the best part entirely up to you: the decoration. Whether you want to paint intricate floral patterns, bold geometric shapes, or your favorite quirky quotes, we supply all the tools and colorful inspiration you need to make it happen. It’s a wonderful way to unwind solo, catch up with friends, or enjoy a creative hour of family crafting.

Participants learn core principles through short presentations, then work through case studies, small-group discussions, and structured role plays to cement their skills. Everyone who completes the day is certified by Welcome Brain as a Neurodiversity First Responder, giving them a recognised role within their organisation. Fresh Stat: Events - Fresh Start EVENTS Help us by taking part in a challenge There are lots of different events you can organise or take part in to help support our work. Whether you are looking to take part in a physical challenge or do something you enjoy socially whilst raising funds for your favourite charity, there are many different ways you can raise funds and awareness for Fresh Start. Run the Edinburgh marathon, take part in the Scottish 5k or 10k, get grubby at Tough Mudder, get sponsored to climb a mountain, hold a bake sale, do a sponsored silence, take part in a game-a-thon, the ideas are endless and we would love to hear yours! You can even run your own event! Every little helps and we would love to support you in running your own fundraiser for Fresh Start, whether that’s providing promotional materials for a coffee morning, bake sale, or crafting evening, to something bigger! Check out some great ideas of how you can raise funds in your own unique way! We would love you to choose Fresh Start for any event you are taking part in and can support you in the sponsorship process and promote your efforts and progress through our social media channels if you wish. You can download our sponsorship form, with Gift Aid declaration here. If you are interested in taking part in any of the above, or for further information on how you can fundraise in support of Fresh Start, please contact us at admin@freshstartweb.org.uk - you can also download this poster to display at your fundraising event!
